document_title: Trade Marks Act, 1999 and Trade Marks Rules, 2017
issuing_authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (IP India)
snippet: Section 9 establishes absolute grounds for refusal of registration. Generic or descriptive Sanskrit or botanical names of Ayurvedic herbs (e.g., 'Ashwagandha', 'Triphala', 'Neem', 'Brahmi', 'Chyawanprash') cannot be registered as word marks in Class 5 (Medicines) or Class 3 (Cosmetics) because they describe the nature, quality, or intended purpose of the goods. However, distinctive brand names combined with herbal ingredients or unique composite device logos are registrable.
keywords: trademark class 5, trademark class 3, descriptive generic terms, section 9 refusal, ayurvedic brand name, device mark

document_title: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
snippet: Protects agricultural and manufactured goods possessing qualities, reputation or characteristics attributable to their geographical origin. Key registered Ayurvedic botanical GIs include Navara Rice (medicinal rice used in Panchakarma), Nilambur Teak, Kangra Tea, Kashmir Saffron, and Malabar Pepper. Authorized users can leverage GI certification for premium export positioning.
keywords: geographical indication, gi registration, navara rice, kashmir saffron, authorized user, regional reputation
